narrative.title: Balancing the Trading Floor's Bracket Ledger
narrative.scenario: A market maker prints order tickets where every open bracket must be closed by a matching one, and the compliance desk wants the full catalogue of well-formed ticket templates exactly n brackets long. A template is built one character at a time: an open bracket may be printed while any remain unopened, and a close bracket may only follow if an open one is still pending. The builder branches on those two rules until every bracket pair is complete.
narrative.inputFormat: An integer n, the number of bracket pairs.
narrative.outputFormat: Every well-formed bracket string of length 2n, in the order the depth-first build produces them.

complexity.optimalTime: O(4^n / sqrt(n)) valid sequences, each costing O(n) to build
complexity.optimalSpace: O(n) recursion depth beyond the output

testCases.explanation: All five ways to interleave three open-close pairs without a close ever leading an open.
One pair admits exactly one template.

hintLevels: Level 1: Never guess a full string — grow it character by character and abandon any prefix that breaks the balance rule.
Level 2: Track two counters. An open may be added while fewer than n are outstanding; a close only while more opens than closes are pending.
Level 3: The recursion stops exactly when both counters hit n — that single landing point guarantees validity, so no post-check is needed.
